title: Final Answer 1
description: Essential Criteria: The response must state that nuclei cannot be composed of protons and electrons.

title: Final Answer 2
description: Essential Criteria: The response must indicate that electrons cannot be bound in the nucleus.

title: Final Answer 3
description: Essential Criteria: The response must mention that the nuclear magnetic moment does not support the existence of electrons in the nucleus.

title: Final Answer 4
description: Essential Criteria: The response must explain that the continuous spectrum contradicts the idea of electrons being inside the nucleus.

title: Statistical Argument
description: Important Criteria: The response should include reasoning based on the statistical nature of nuclei and experimental spin results.

title: Binding Energy Argument
description: Important Criteria: The response should discuss the role of binding energy and the inability of electrons to participate in strong interactions.

title: Magnetic Moment Argument
description: Important Criteria: The response should analyze the nuclear magnetic moment and its implications for the composition of the nucleus.

title: Beta Decay Argument
description: Important Criteria: The response should address the implications of beta decay and the resulting energy spectrum.

title: Common Errors
description: Pitfall Criteria: The response should avoid common errors such as misinterpreting the role of electrons in nuclear processes.
